name: Gello
description: A female demon of Greek and Byzantine tradition, attested as early as Sappho (6th century BC), said to attack pregnant women, newborns, and the unmarried, and the central target of a long-running corpus of apotropaic charms and exorcisms in the Greek-speaking world.

aliases.name: Gelloudes
aliases.meaning: plural form denoting a class of demons

aliases.name: Abyzou
aliases.meaning: from abyssos, 'the deep'; identified with Gello in late antiquity and Byzantine literature

origin: Originally a localized Greek tradition (attested for Sappho on Lesbos), the Gello / gelloudes complex spread throughout the Greek-speaking Byzantine world and, through the 'Legend of Saint Sisinnios', into Coptic, Ethiopic, Armenian, Romanian, Slavonic, Arabic, Syriac, and Hebrew manuscript traditions across the eastern Mediterranean and Near East.
